executive_summary.headline: Right Shift captures an estimated Rs 10,42,000 of the tracked Rs 14,58,200 monthly category revenue by pricing below Rs 90/kg, while products priced over Rs 400/kg show low unit volume.
executive_summary.category_shape: Category pricing spans from Rs 72/kg to Rs 1099/kg across 15 products. Revenue is highly concentrated, with Right Shift holding 71.5% of estimated monthly sales across two SKUs. Out of 15 listings, 9 have no estimated sales volume data available.
key_findings: Right Shift commands Rs 10,42,000 in combined estimated monthly sales across its 5kg (Rs 89.8/kg) and 1kg (Rs 72/kg) SKUs.

Ultra-premium products priced above Rs 400/kg, such as Lo Low Carb (Rs 499/kg) and The Lean Co. (Rs 513.7/kg), record lower monthly revenues of Rs 49,900 and Rs 124,900, alongside mixed consumer feedback on value for money.
9 of the 15 tracked products carry no estimated sales volume or revenue figures in the dataset.
Review feedback across 6 analyzed products shows consistent praise for soft texture and taste, while price resistance appears on SKUs priced above Rs 400/kg.
recommended_actions: Position a new entrant in the mid-premium price band between Rs 180/kg and Rs 250/kg, sitting between Right Shift (Rs 72-89.8/kg) and ultra-premium brands (Rs 400+/kg).
Offer both 1kg and 5kg pack sizes at launch; the 5kg pack size accounts for Rs 8,98,000 of Right Shift's sales versus Rs 1,44,000 for its 1kg pack.
Formulate specifically for soft roti texture and taste to mitigate the 'value for money' negative tags observed in premium competitors like Lo Low Carb (8 mixed tags).

gaps: Clean-label daily wellness packaging in the Rs 150 - 220/kg price range, bridging the gap between low-cost commercial packs and high-cost clinical fitness pouches.
positioning_whitespace.read: An entrant priced between Rs 180/kg and Rs 220/kg with clean lifestyle branding can avoid direct price competition with Right Shift without triggering the price sensitivity seen above Rs 400/kg.
